coverage: Selected US patent developments; curated snapshot, not a complete citator or live news feed.

items.title: USPTO supplements eligibility-declaration guidance
items.summary: The memorandum adds a flowchart and best practices for subject matter eligibility declarations under Rule 132. It supplements the April 2026 memorandum and expressly says it introduces no new practice or procedure.
items.practice_note: In prosecution, identify the particular eligibility proposition supported by the declaration and distinguish factual evidence from argument. This is agency guidance, not a new district-court eligibility standard.
items.review_status: source checked; legal characterization pending attorney review

items.title: USPTO updates Director Review process guidance
items.summary: The USPTO identifies June 29, 2026 as the update date for section 3.B of its Director Review process page. The page provides implementation details for review under 37 CFR 42.75.
items.practice_note: Consult the current request requirements and the operative order before planning Director Review. A review request or its denial is not a binary patent-validity outcome.
items.review_status: source checked; legal characterization pending attorney review

items.title: Additional PTAB discretionary institution considerations
items.summary: The USPTO identifies US manufacturing, related investment, and small-business petitioner circumstances as additional considerations in discretionary institution decisions for IPR and PGR proceedings.
items.practice_note: Check the memorandum’s applicability to the patent-owner briefing deadline. Institution discretion and the merits of a final written decision must remain separate in outcome datasets.
items.pinpoint: Announcement, numbered considerations 1–3 and applicability paragraph

items.title: EcoFactor: support for a royalty expert’s license-based rate
items.summary: The en banc court held that the licenses at issue did not support the expert’s conclusion that prior licensees agreed to the asserted per-unit royalty rate, and found an abuse of discretion in failing to exclude that testimony.
items.practice_note: Inspect the operative license terms and the factual foundation for the proposed royalty rate. This damages-evidence ruling does not itself establish infringement or validity.
items.review_status: source checked; subsequent treatment requires separate verification
